questions.question: Runner A runs at a speed of 8 m/s while Runner B runs at 5 m/s. Which statement correctly compares their journey over a fixed 100-metre distance?
options: Runner A takes less time because a greater speed requires less time to cover a certain distance.
Runner B takes less time because lower speeds allow more efficient energy use.
Both take the same time because the distance is identical.
Runner A takes more time because greater speed increases the distance traveled.

questions.question: If Drone X flies at a speed of 12 m/s and Drone Y flies at 8 m/s, what is the result if they both fly for a set time of exactly 15 seconds?
options: Drone Y travels a greater distance because it has less air resistance.
Drone X travels a greater distance because a higher speed covers more distance in a certain time.
Both drones travel the same distance because the flight duration is identical.
Drone X travels a shorter distance because higher speeds reduce the time of the flight.

questions.question: A remote-controlled car travels a total distance of 24 metres in a time of 8 seconds. What is its speed?
options: 3 m/s, calculated by dividing 24 metres by 8 seconds.
192 m/s, calculated by multiplying 24 metres by 8 seconds.
0.33 m/s, calculated by dividing 8 seconds by 24 metres.
16 m/s, calculated by subtracting 8 seconds from 24 metres.

questions.question: A hockey puck is sliding across ice. If a player uses their stick to apply a resultant force in the direction of its movement, what is the immediate effect?
options: The puck will continue at the same speed but change its mass.
The speed of the puck will change.
The puck will immediately stop moving.
The puck's speed will remain completely constant despite the force.

questions.question: A constant resultant force acts on a trolley for 5 seconds. What happens to the trolley's speed during this 5-second interval?
options: The speed changes only at the exact moment the force is first applied.
The speed remains constant until the force stops, then it changes.
The speed changes continuously throughout the entire time the force is acting.
The speed increases for the first second and then stays constant.

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, Line A has a very steep positive gradient, while Line B has a gentle positive gradient. What does this tell you about their movement?
options: Object A is moving slower than Object B.
Object A is moving faster than Object B.
Object A has travelled a shorter total distance than Object B.
Object A has been moving for a longer duration than Object B.

questions.question: Two balls of identical mass but different shapes—one crumpled into a tight ball and one spread out as a flat sheet—are dropped. Why do they experience different drag forces at the same speed?
options: Drag force depends only on the mass of the falling object.
Drag force depends on the speed and shape of the falling object.
Drag force is entirely constant and does not depend on speed or shape.
Drag force only depends on the gravitational pull of the Earth.

questions.question: A skydiver falls through the air and reaches terminal velocity. Which statement correctly describes the forces acting on the skydiver at this point?
options: The upward drag force is greater than the downward gravitational force.
The downward gravitational force is greater than the upward drag force.
The drag and gravitational forces are equal in size.
There are no forces at all acting on the skydiver at terminal velocity.

questions.question: How does deploying a parachute affect a falling skydiver's terminal velocity?
options: It increases the terminal velocity by reducing the drag force.
It decreases the terminal velocity by increasing the drag force.
It keeps the terminal velocity the same but increases the gravitational force.
It eliminates terminal velocity entirely so they continue to accelerate forever.

questions.question: A parachutist has reached their constant top speed during a descent. How does the size of the drag force on the parachute compare to the force of gravity on the jumper?
options: The drag force is larger than the force of gravity.
The drag force is smaller than the force of gravity.
The drag force is the same size as the force of gravity.
The drag force is zero, and only gravity is acting.

questions.question: A section of a distance-time graph is represented by a perfectly horizontal, level line. What does this indicate about the object's motion?
options: The object is moving at a high, constant speed.
The object is stationary with no movement.
The object is accelerating rapidly.
The object is moving backwards toward its starting point.

questions.question: On a distance-time graph representing a journey, Section X has an upward sloping line, while Section Y has a downward sloping line. What do these sections show?
options: Section X shows the object speeding up, while Section Y shows it slowing down.
Section X and Section Y show movement in opposite directions.
Section X shows movement forward, while Section Y shows the object is stationary.
Both sections show movement in the same direction but at different speeds.

questions.question: A student is measuring the position of a moving toy car against a metre ruler. To ensure an accurate measurement, where should the student position their eyes?
options: At an angle from the side to get a wider view of the ruler.
In line with the point of observation.
Slightly above and to the left of the car's front edge.
Anywhere, as long as the ruler is well-lit.

questions.question: During an experiment measuring the time it takes a trolley to roll down a ramp, why is it beneficial to take several repeat readings instead of just one?
options: It completely eliminates all systematic errors in the stopwatch.
It reduces the effect of random errors.
It increases the gravitational force acting on the trolley.
It changes the average speed of the trolley on each run.

questions.question: A student records the following times for a trolley run: 1.2s, 1.3s, 1.2s, 3.5s, 1.3s. How should they handle the 3.5s reading when calculating the average time?
options: Include it in the average calculation because all data points must be used.
Add it to the lowest reading and then divide by two.
Do not use it in calculations because it is an anomalous reading.
Replace it with a value of zero before calculating the average.

questions.question: A wooden block is being pulled to the right across a rough table. In which direction does the friction force act on the block?
options: To the right, helping the block to slide.
Against the direction of movement, which is to the left.
Upwards, opposing the weight of the block.
Downwards, pulling the block into the table.

questions.question: A spacecraft is moving through deep space where there is no gravity and no friction. If its engines are turned off, what will happen to its motion?
options: It will immediately slow down and come to a complete stop.
It will continue to move at a steady speed in a straight line.
It will curve in a circle due to its remaining momentum.
It will slowly lose speed until it eventually stops.

questions.question: A student looks at a single, specific point on a distance-time graph. What information does this single point directly describe?
options: The instantaneous speed of the object at that exact moment.
The total average speed of the entire journey.
Where the object is at a specific point in time.
The acceleration of the object at that moment.

questions.question: Why does streamlining a submarine make it move more efficiently through the water?
options: It increases the gravitational force pulling it downwards.
It reduces how much fluid needs to be pushed out of the way for the object to move.
It increases the surface area to maximize water resistance.
It allows the submarine to float higher without using its engines.

questions.question: As a speedboat increases its speed from 10 km/h to 50 km/h, what happens to the drag force acting on its hull from the water?
options: The drag force decreases because the boat rises out of the water.
The drag force remains constant because the fluid density is unchanged.
The drag force increases with speed.
The drag force becomes zero once the boat reaches its top speed.
